head_commit.message:
Batch synchronous HBM output allocations in TpuRawClient.

Dispatching executables with thousands of HBM outputs currently invokes `TpuRawClient::AllocateRawBufferForExecute` per output, acquiring the TPU allocator and shared-memory locks once per buffer across concurrent device dispatch threads.

Override `TpuRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` to fulfill HBM output batches through `System::TryAllocateBuffers` in a single synchronous batch when no deferred allocations are active, falling back to `PjRtRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` on OOM, backpressure, or non-HBM memory spaces so each buffer retains an independent lifetime and existing OOM recovery behavior is preserved.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix use-after-free from orphaned async kernel compilation futures

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix use-after-free from orphaned async kernel compilation futures

Asynchronous kernel compilation tasks scheduled via `KernelCompiler` capture
`IrEmitterContext*` and `BufferAssignment*` (owned by `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`)
as well as `CubinCustomKernelCompiler*`. Returning early on an error before
awaiting all launched futures allows worker threads on the compilation thread
pool to dereference these objects after they have been destroyed.

Fix three error paths that could orphan in-flight compilation futures:
- In `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, await both `future_thunks` and
  `future_constants_binary` before propagating any error from either future.
- In `ThunkEmitter::EmitConditional`, resolve the predicate allocation slice
  before launching `EmitHloComputation` futures for the branch computations.
- In `EmitBitonicSort`, return a `Future<std::unique_ptr<Thunk>>` from
  `emit_thunk` and collect all futures into `thunks` so `tsl::JoinFutures`
  always awaits previously launched bitonic sort kernels even if a later stage
  fails.

name: CI
display_title: Own constant content when the HloModule is not embedded

head_commit.message:
Own constant content when the HloModule is not embedded

Non-scalar constants are not emitted as initializers in the LLVM IR. Instead the executable keeps their content and copies it to the device on the first execution. That content is a `DenseDataIntermediate` which aliases the literal of the constant instruction in the HloModule. With `CompileOptions::embed_hlo_module=false`, `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` doesn't move the module into the `GpuExecutable`, so the module (and with it the literal) gets destroyed at the end of `RunBackend` and the constants point to freed memory. This went unnoticed so far because the only users of that option (the autotuner and the Triton numerics verifier) compile clones that share their literals with a source module that stays alive.

So this change makes the constants own a copy of their content in `RunBackend`, but only if the module doesn't get embedded. I made the decision there because that's the place that decides to drop the module. The default path (module embedded) keeps aliasing the literals, so there is no extra copy and no additional memory use. The new `DenseDataIntermediate::ToOwned()` only copies aliased data, so sub-byte constants (which are already packed into an owned buffer) don't get copied a second time.

There are two new tests in `xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler_test.cc`. The first one compiles a module with an f32 and an s4 constant without embedding it, makes sure the module is gone, and then checks the constant contents and the result of an execution. Without the fix it reports a heap-use-after-free under ASAN. The second one doesn't need ASAN: it checks that the constant content aliases the module's literal if and only if the module gets embedded, which also pins the no-copy behavior of the default path.

display_title: Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff cquery tag filters

head_commit.message:
Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff cquery tag filters

`Build.bazel_command` always appends `-manual` to `--build_tag_filters` when running a test or build with a `bazel-diff` target pattern file, but `get_cquery_command_options` in `build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` did not include `-manual`. Because `cquery --universe_scope` evaluates wildcard patterns without filtering `manual` targets by default, `bazel-diff` analyzed `manual` targets (such as GPU backend `test_suite` rules on CPU jobs) and included them in the impacted targets list.

So this change appends `-manual` to `--build_tag_filters` in `get_cquery_command_options`. Also, in `xla/tests/build_defs.bzl`, it forwards `tags + ["manual"]` to the fallback empty `strict_cc_test` in `xla_test` when `test_names` is empty, matching the `test_suite` branch.

Add cuda-only and gpu tags to //xla/tsl/cuda stub rules

The `textual_hdrs` attribute on the CUDA stub `cc_library` targets in `//xla/tsl/cuda` unconditionally references the generated `.inc` files from `cuda_stub`. name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Optionally register host memory in a shared CUDA context.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Optionally register host memory in a shared CUDA context.

`cuMemHostUnregister` synchronizes the context that the memory was registered in while holding that context's lock: it waits for all of the context's streams, and other threads can't launch work or enqueue copies in the context meanwhile. With memory registered in a device's primary context, this can deadlock with an in-flight collective. The device's side of the collective is already enqueued, but the peer can't launch its side until a copy that has to be enqueued in the same primary context is enqueued, and that copy waits for the context lock held by `cuMemHostUnregister`.

With `XLA_CUDA_REGISTER_HOST_MEMORY_IN_SHARED_CONTEXT=1`, `CudaExecutor::HostMemoryRegister`/`HostMemoryUnregister` register and unregister host memory in one context shared by all executors in the process instead of the executor's primary context:

- The env var is read and the shared context is created on the first registration, on the device of the executor doing it, and the context lives until the process exits. In PjRt that is always the client's first device, since `DmaMap` and the pinned host memory allocator register through it; the device only determines which GPU holds the context's memory. It's created with `cuCtxCreate_v4` (same signature in CUDA 12 and 13 headers; needs a 12.5+ driver), with the stack size limit set to 0 since no kernels run in it. If it can't be created, every executor registers in its primary context.
- It has no streams, so unregistering memory registered in it waits for nothing and doesn't block any primary context, whichever context the caller has current. The memory is registered as portable, so it's still treated as pinned by every context, and one shared context is enough for all devices.
- Registration pushes the shared context on top of the activated primary context and pops it afterwards, so the calling thread is left in the same state as without the flag.
- Unregistering no longer implicitly waits for work in the registering device's primary context. It never waited for work on other devices, so callers must already make sure the memory is no longer used before unregistering it.

The shared context costs a few hundred MiB of device memory, so the flag is off by default.

Adds `cuCtxCreate_v4` to `cuda.symbols`.

name: CI
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

head_commit.message:
PR #52290: [ROCm][IFRT IR] Accept the ROCm platform in IFRT IR compilation passes

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52290

📝 Summary of Changes

`IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass` and `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass`
recognize only the TPU, CUDA and CPU platforms (plus `host` in the verifier). So
compiling an IFRT IR program whose atom programs run on ROCm devices fails:
- `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass::initialize` logs `Unsupported platform: rocm`
  and fails.
- `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass` reports
  `'ifrt.Call' op Unsupported platform for call op: rocm`.
`BasicAtomProgramCompiler` already accepts `rocm`, so these two passes were the only
blockers. This change accepts `xla::RocmName()` wherever `xla::CudaName()` is accepted.

🎯 Justification

Found while compiling Shardy MPMD programs (lowered with `jaxlib._sdy_mpmd.lower_to_ifrt`)
with `IfrtIrProgramCompiler` on the ROCm PJRT plugin.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply:
✨ New Feature,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Please measure and include speedups for one of the public HLOs in
`compiler/xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo/`.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- New `ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency_rocm.mlir`: an all-ROCm call passes, and a
  call spanning ROCm and CPU devices reports the single-platform error. It is a
  separate file because the existing test's RUN line fixes the device-to-platform
  mapping, which its out-of-range device case depends on.
- New RUN line in `ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir` with
  `platform_names=rocm,rocm`, reusing the existing Shardy checks.

      //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency.mlir.test \
      //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir.test
All three pass. With the two pass changes reverted, both new ROCm cases fail with the
errors above.

display_title: Add `TraceMeFilter::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback = 1` in `trace_filter_utils.h` and clear bit 1 (`~(1ULL << tsl::profiler::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback)`) in `kTraceMeDefaultFilterMask` in `traceme.h`.

head_commit.message:
Add `TraceMeFilter::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback = 1` in `trace_filter_utils.h` and clear bit 1 (`~(1ULL << tsl::profiler::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback)`) in `kTraceMeDefaultFilterMask` in `traceme.h`.

This allows profiling sessions configured with `host_traceme_filter_mask = (1ULL << 1)` to record exclusively `kTraceHostEnqueueCallback`-tagged host enqueue and callback events while leaving unfiltered and `kTraceMemory`-filtered sessions unchanged.

name: CI
display_title: Batch synchronous HBM output allocations in TpuRawClient.

head_commit.message:
Batch synchronous HBM output allocations in TpuRawClient.

Dispatching executables with thousands of HBM outputs currently invokes `TpuRawClient::AllocateRawBufferForExecute` per output, acquiring the TPU allocator and shared-memory locks once per buffer across concurrent device dispatch threads.

Override `TpuRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` to fulfill HBM output batches through `System::TryAllocateBuffers` in a single synchronous batch when no deferred allocations or test fault-injection hooks are active, falling back to `PjRtRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` on OOM, backpressure, or non-HBM memory spaces so each buffer retains an independent lifetime and existing OOM recovery behavior is preserved.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012864658

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] PR 3/3: Skip re-recording unchanged collectives in command buffers

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] [CUDA] Skip re-recording unchanged collectives in command buffers

- With COLLECTIVES and non-persistent buffer allocations, Initialize
  re-records every command buffer that holds a collective on every
  execution, so that all participants record their collectives together.
- New flag --xla_gpu_command_buffer_skip_unchanged_collectives (default
  off): when every participant is in this process, the participants agree
  through a host rendezvous and record again only if one of them has to:
  not warmed up, not recorded yet, profiling, or a buffer of these
  collectives moved. The flag is a field of CommandBufferThunkOptions.

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] PR 2/3: Record only the changed allocations in CommandBufferThunk

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] [CUDA] Record only the changed allocations in CommandBufferThunk

- ChangedAllocations returns the non-persistent allocations of the
  commands whose address differs from the recorded one, or that were never
  recorded, and AllocationChanged is its per-allocation check.
- UpdateBufferAllocations records exactly those, without building a list
  of all dynamic allocations on every execution, and no longer lists an
  allocation twice the first time it is recorded.

name: CI
display_title: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

- The flag puts temp buffers in memory space kTempBuffer, but only CUDA
  registered an allocator for it. On ROCm, execution failed with "No
  allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter ... memory space 2".
- On ROCm, register a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for
  kTempBuffer, named GPU_tempbuffer_<n>_bfc. Only temp buffers use it, so
  they keep the same address across executions.
- Next to a preallocated default pool, the temp pool gets the device
  memory that the default pool's start fraction leaves, like the
  collective pool; MemFractionLeft computes that remainder for both.
  Without preallocation it keeps the default pool's limit. Creating the
  client fails with a clear error if nothing is left for the temp pool.
- CreateBFCAllocator takes a name prefix (default "GPU", so existing
  pools keep GPU_<n>_bfc).
- In SharedPoolAnchorsCollectiveMemoryAtLowerEnd, convert device
  addresses to uintptr_t with reinterpret_cast instead of
  absl::bit_cast. The clang 18 static analyzer crashes comparing
  bit_cast pointer values, which fails clang-tidy on any change to
  this file.
- Update the flag's help text and add tests.

name: CI
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Optionally register host memory in a shared CUDA context.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Optionally register host memory in a shared CUDA context.

`cuMemHostUnregister` synchronizes the context that the memory was registered in while holding that context's lock: it waits for all of the context's streams, and other threads can't launch work or enqueue copies in the context meanwhile. With memory registered in a device's primary context, this can deadlock with an in-flight collective. The device's side of the collective is already enqueued, but the peer can't launch its side until a copy that has to be enqueued in the same primary context is enqueued, and that copy waits for the context lock held by `cuMemHostUnregister`.

With `XLA_CUDA_REGISTER_HOST_MEMORY_IN_SHARED_CONTEXT=1`, `CudaExecutor::HostMemoryRegister`/`HostMemoryUnregister` register and unregister host memory in one context shared by all executors in the process instead of the executor's primary context:

- The env var is read and the shared context is created on the first registration, on the device of the executor doing it, and the context lives until the process exits. In PjRt that is always the client's first device, since `DmaMap` and the pinned host memory allocator register through it; the device only determines which GPU holds the context's memory. It's created with `cuCtxCreate_v4` (same signature in CUDA 12 and 13 headers; needs a 12.5+ driver), with the stack size limit set to 0 since no kernels run in it. If it can't be created, every executor registers in its primary context.
- It has no streams, so unregistering memory registered in it waits for nothing and doesn't block any primary context, whichever context the caller has current. The memory is registered as portable, so it's still treated as pinned by every context, and one shared context is enough for all devices.
- Registration pushes the shared context on top of the activated primary context and pops it afterwards, so the calling thread is left in the same state as without the flag.
- Unregistering no longer implicitly waits for work in the registering device's primary context. It never waited for work on other devices, so callers must already make sure the memory is no longer used before unregistering it.

The shared context costs a few hundred MiB of device memory, so the flag is off by default.

Adds `cuCtxCreate_v4` to `cuda.symbols`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013104834

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix use-after-free from orphaned async kernel compilation futures

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix use-after-free from orphaned async kernel compilation futures

Asynchronous kernel compilation tasks scheduled via `KernelCompiler` capture
`IrEmitterContext*` and `BufferAssignment*` (owned by `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`)
as well as `CubinCustomKernelCompiler*`. Returning early on an error before
awaiting all launched futures allows worker threads on the compilation thread
pool to dereference these objects after they have been destroyed.

Fix three error paths that could orphan in-flight compilation futures:
- In `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, await both `future_thunks` and
  `future_constants_binary` before propagating any error from either future.
- In `ThunkEmitter::EmitConditional`, resolve the predicate allocation slice
  before launching `EmitHloComputation` futures for the branch computations.
- In `EmitBitonicSort`, return a `Future<std::unique_ptr<Thunk>>` from
  `emit_thunk` and collect all futures into `thunks` so `tsl::JoinFutures`
  always awaits previously launched bitonic sort kernels even if a later stage
  fails.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013744240

name: CI
display_title: Fix rounding and consistency of casts to f8e8m0fnu across ml_dtypes and XLA

head_commit.message:
Fix rounding and consistency of casts to f8e8m0fnu across ml_dtypes and XLA

Conversions to `float8_e8m0fnu` rounded `(2^-127, 1.5 * 2^-127)` up to `2^-126`
instead of `2^-127` in `ml_dtypes` and XLA `EmitFloatConversion`.
`EmitFloatConversion` also mapped positive `float64` values below `2^-127` to
`NaN`. `HloEvaluator` flushed unpacked `2^-127` to `+0.0f` during `F8E8M0FNU`
min and max on worker threads with denormals flushed to zero.

Encode zeroless targets with normal precision in biased exponent 0 across
`ml_dtypes::ConvertImpl` and `EmitFloatConversion`, clamping smaller positive
inputs to code `0x00`. Preserve `2^-127` and `NaN` in `HloEvaluator` min and
max, and add `ml_dtypes` and XLA tests covering the lowest binade.

name: CI
display_title: Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

Dispatching executables with many outputs currently invokes `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` and constructs a debug-annotation closure once per non-aliased output leaf, while `ExecuteOptions::use_output_arena` couples all output buffer lifetimes to the longest-lived output.

Add `PjRtRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` (defaulting to a loop over `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` so existing backends preserve their behavior) and group non-aliased output allocations by memory space in `CommonPjRtClient::AllocateOutputBuffersWithInputReuse` so backends can allocate decoupled output buffers in a single batch per memory space.

name: CI
display_title: Batch synchronous HBM output allocations in TpuRawClient.

head_commit.message:
Batch synchronous HBM output allocations in TpuRawClient.

Dispatching executables with thousands of HBM outputs currently invokes `TpuRawClient::AllocateRawBufferForExecute` per output, acquiring the TPU allocator and shared-memory locks once per buffer across concurrent device dispatch threads.

Override `TpuRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` to fulfill HBM output batches through `System::TryAllocateBuffers` in a single synchronous batch when no deferred allocations or test fault-injection hooks are active, falling back to `PjRtRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` on OOM, backpressure, or non-HBM memory spaces so each buffer retains an independent lifetime and existing OOM recovery behavior is preserved.

never changes anywhere in the program, but other kernels write these buffers.

xla_llvm_enable_invariant_load_metadata flag is deprecated.

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

head_commit.message:
Round casts to f8e8m0fnu in the lowest binade to nearest

ml_dtypes ConvertImpl, XLA EmitF32ToF8e8m0fnu, and XLA EmitFloatConversion
rounded inputs in (2^-127, 1.5 * 2^-127) up to 2^-126 (code 0x01) instead of

display_title: [XLA] Fold collectives on uniform constants in AlgebraicSimplifier.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fold collectives on uniform constants in AlgebraicSimplifier.

`AlgebraicSimplifier` already folds `all-gather`, `all-to-all`, `all-reduce`, and `reduce-scatter` (`min`/`max`/`sum`) when their operand is `broadcast(scalar_constant)`. Extend this to plain uniform `constant` operands—such as scalar (`pred[]`) and single-element (`pred[1]`) constants, which are not canonicalized into broadcasts.

For example, this now folds to `%x` in a single pass:
```
%ar0 = pred[1] all-reduce(pred[1] constant({true})), to_apply=min
%ar1 = pred[]  all-reduce(pred[] reshape(%ar0)), to_apply=min
%out = pred[]  and(%x, %ar1)
```

name: CI
display_title: Avoid unconditional filter mask creation in ConvolutionGroupConverter

head_commit.message:
Avoid unconditional filter mask creation in ConvolutionGroupConverter

`ConvolutionVisitor::HandleConvolution` previously called `ExpandedFilterShape`
and `GetExpandedFilterMask` before checking whether filter expansion would
actually be used (`group_size == 1 && (!is_cost_viable_ || filter_expansion_)`).
When `group_size > 1` or `filter_expansion_ == false`, this emitted dead mask
instructions and materialized `group_count * group_size` elements in host memory
via `GetMaskIds`, overflowing 32-bit `int` loop counters or exhausting memory on
large feature dimensions.

Move `ExpandedFilterShape` and `GetExpandedFilterMask` into the filter-expansion
branch and widen the loop counters in `GetMaskIds` to `int64_t`.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Add XLA linking through ifrt::Compiler::Compile for pjrt_ifrt

This change adds experimental support for linking PjRtRelocatables
through IFRT via the ifrt::Compiler::Compile API. The basic idea is to
embed the relocatables into the IFRT compile options, and if they're
present, to invoke the linker via the PjRtPhaseCompiler API and ignore
the input module.

This is a little hacky, but avoids any IFRT API updates while
relocatables are still experimental.

As an additional note, this change exposes the GetPjRtCompiler function
as part of the PjRt public API. Normally callers use PjRtCompile, but
in order to invoke the API we really need access to the PjRtCompiler to
get at the PjRtPhaseCompiler.

display_title: Group output buffer allocations by memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Group output buffer allocations by memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

`CommonPjRtClient::AllocateOutputBuffersWithInputReuse` currently scans `device->memory_spaces()` on every non-aliased output leaf, allocates non-arena buffers inline during the loop, and collects arena allocations into an unordered pointer-keyed `absl::flat_hash_map<PjRtMemorySpace*, ...>`. Preparing for per-memory-space batched output allocation requires deterministic grouping of pending output allocations across both the default and arena paths.

Collect non-aliased output allocations into an `absl::InlinedVector` ordered deterministically by first-seen memory space `kind_id`, resolving `PjRtMemorySpace*` once per distinct `kind_id`, and execute either the per-output or arena allocation loop over those grouped entries with no functional change.

name: CI
display_title: PR #52439: [tsl] Use non-const CRTP parameter in ReferenceCounted for RCReference<const T>

head_commit.message:
PR #52439: [tsl] Use non-const CRTP parameter in ReferenceCounted for RCReference<const T>

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52439

fc3777183a added `RCReference<const T>` support through a separate `ReferenceCounted<const SubClass>` specialization. Types had to opt in by writing `class Foo : public ReferenceCounted<const Foo>`.

**Why.** A CRTP parameter should always be the plain derived type. Constness belongs to the holder, not to the base class: `ReferenceCounted<T>` defines how `T` is counted and destroyed, and `RCReference<const T>` limits access to `T` the same way `std::shared_ptr<const T>` does.

**Design.** I removed the specialization. In the primary template, `AddRef()`/`DropRef()`/`Destroy()` are now `const` and the counter is `mutable`, so any `ReferenceCounted` type works with `RCReference<const T>`. `ReferenceCounted<const T>` is now rejected with a `static_assert`.

**Prior art.** `boost::intrusive_ref_counter<DerivedT>` takes a non-const `DerivedT` and stores a `mutable` counter. Its `intrusive_ptr_add_ref`/`intrusive_ptr_release` take `const intrusive_ref_counter*` and delete through `static_cast<const DerivedT*>`, which is why `boost::intrusive_ptr<const T>` works for any derived type ([intrusive_ref_counter](https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_62_0/libs/smart_ptr/intrusive_ref_counter.html), [intrusive_ptr](https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_62_0/libs/smart_ptr/intrusive_ptr.html)).

Copybara import of the project:

--

[TSL] Use non-const CRTP parameter in ReferenceCounted for RCReference<const T>

Remove the ReferenceCounted<const SubClass> specialization. The CRTP parameter
must always be the plain derived type; constness belongs to the holder, i.e.
RCReference<const T>, as with std::shared_ptr<const T> and
boost::intrusive_ptr<const T>.

Make AddRef()/DropRef()/Destroy() const and the reference counter mutable in
the primary template (same as boost::intrusive_ref_counter), so every
ReferenceCounted type can be managed via RCReference<const T>. Reject
ReferenceCounted<const T> with a static_assert.

Merging this change closes #52439

name: CI
display_title: PR #52439: [tsl] Use non-const CRTP parameter in ReferenceCounted for RCReference<const T>

head_commit.message:
PR #52439: [tsl] Use non-const CRTP parameter in ReferenceCounted for RCReference<const T>

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52439

fc3777183a added `RCReference<const T>` support through a separate `ReferenceCounted<const SubClass>` specialization. Types had to opt in by writing `class Foo : public ReferenceCounted<const Foo>`.

**Why.** A CRTP parameter should always be the plain derived type. Constness belongs to the holder, not to the base class: `ReferenceCounted<T>` defines how `T` is counted and destroyed, and `RCReference<const T>` limits access to `T` the same way `std::shared_ptr<const T>` does.

**Design.** I removed the specialization. In the primary template, `AddRef()`/`DropRef()`/`Destroy()` are now `const` and the counter is `mutable`, so any `ReferenceCounted` type works with `RCReference<const T>`. `ReferenceCounted<const T>` is now rejected with a `static_assert`.

**Prior art.** `boost::intrusive_ref_counter<DerivedT>` takes a non-const `DerivedT` and stores a `mutable` counter. Its `intrusive_ptr_add_ref`/`intrusive_ptr_release` take `const intrusive_ref_counter*` and delete through `static_cast<const DerivedT*>`, which is why `boost::intrusive_ptr<const T>` works for any derived type ([intrusive_ref_counter](https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_62_0/libs/smart_ptr/intrusive_ref_counter.html), [intrusive_ptr](https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_62_0/libs/smart_ptr/intrusive_ptr.html)).

Copybara import of the project:

--
0e935ff7eb477aa374efe42ccc680fee93b035c9 by Eugene Zhulenev <ezhulenev@openxla.org>:

[TSL] Use non-const CRTP parameter in ReferenceCounted for RCReference<const T>

Remove the ReferenceCounted<const SubClass> specialization. The CRTP parameter
must always be the plain derived type; constness belongs to the holder, i.e.
RCReference<const T>, as with std::shared_ptr<const T> and
boost::intrusive_ptr<const T>.

Make AddRef()/DropRef()/Destroy() const and the reference counter mutable in
the primary template (same as boost::intrusive_ref_counter), so every
ReferenceCounted type can be managed via RCReference<const T>. Reject
ReferenceCounted<const T> with a static_assert.

Merging this change closes #52439

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

TreeReductionRewriter splits large reductions into a reduce-window followed by
a reduce. CPU fusion did not accept kReduceWindow, so the input of the
reduce-window was always materialized.

Allow fusing producers into a reduce-window if its windows do not overlap and
are not dilated, so every input element is read once. A reduce-window is never
fused into its consumer. Make ReusesOperandElements return false for the array
operands of such a reduce-window, as it already does for kReduce. Also treat a
max reduce-window like a max reduce when looking for the softmax shift pattern.

display_title: Support `tsl::RCReference` ownership for `xla::MultiSliceConfig` on `CompileOptions`

head_commit.message:
Support `tsl::RCReference` ownership for `xla::MultiSliceConfig` on `CompileOptions`

`xla::CompileOptions::multi_slice_config` currently stores a non-owning `const MultiSliceConfig*`, leaving callers responsible for keeping `MultiSliceConfig` instances alive across compilation and executable lifetimes.

Add transitional `const`-qualified `AddRef`, `DropRef`, and `IsUnique` methods on `xla::MultiSliceConfig` along with `xla::MultiSliceConfigRef` (`tsl::RCReference<const MultiSliceConfig>`) so `tsl::RCReference`, `tsl::MakeRef`, and `tsl::FormRef` work immediately while unmigrated `std::unique_ptr`, `std::shared_ptr`, and stack-allocated configs still destroy cleanly without tripping `tsl::ReferenceCounted`'s destructor assertion. On `CompileOptions`, add `owned_multi_slice_config` plus `set_multi_slice_config` and `get_multi_slice_config` accessors that mirror the raw pointer to `multi_slice_config` while downstream callers migrate.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015038979

display_title: Block scaled and structured sparse matmuls need extra operands (scales,

head_commit.message:
Block scaled and structured sparse matmuls need extra operands (scales,
zero points, sparsity indices) next to lhs and rhs. A separate opcode
keeps kDot a plain binary op and lets backends rewrite the extended form
early.

kDotGeneral takes lhs, rhs and at least one metadata operand, with dot
dimension numbers, a SparsityConfig and a BlockScalingConfig. It reuses
the existing HloInstructionProto fields. The verifier rejects a
dot-general without metadata operands; a plain dot must stay a kDot.

TensorBlockScalingConfig gains an optional per dimension block_sizes field
to support padded scale use-cases.

name: CI
display_title: Fill only the padding when linearizing tiled arrays.

head_commit.message:
Fill only the padding when linearizing tiled arrays.

`TiledLinearizer::LinearizeUsingTransposeInto` filled the whole destination buffer with the padding word whenever the array had any padding, and `TransposePlan::Execute` then overwrote almost all of it with the elements. This single-threaded fill runs before the possibly multi-threaded transpose and doubles the memory traffic of linearization.

Fill only the bytes that the transpose does not write: everything but the complete tiles for 2D tilings, everything but each row's elements for 1D tilings, and everything past the elements for rank-1 or untiled arrays. The geometry comes from the `TransposePlan`, and if it disagrees with `TransposePlan::OutputNumElems()` the whole buffer is filled as before. Zero padding is written with `memset`, and NaN padding keeps its previous byte pattern, so the output is bit-identical. The scratch buffer used for sub-tile packed sub-byte types is no longer pre-filled either.

New tests linearize into buffers that initially hold the padding pattern or one of two poison patterns and require identical bytes, so any byte that is left unwritten fails them.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014815077

display_title: Improve `LatencyHidingScheduler` memory-limit reruns in three ways:

head_commit.message:
Improve `LatencyHidingScheduler` memory-limit reruns in three ways:
- Restore the original input schedule (and invalidate `AsyncTracker` caches)
  before every retry so trials differ only in `SchedulerConfig`.
- Evaluate peak non-parameter default-memory-space usage across all rerun modes
  via whole-module `HeapSimulator` (`GlobalDecreasingSizeBestFitHeap` with
  spatial packing) whenever `rerun > 0` and `memory_limit` is finite, capturing
  heap fragmentation and cross-computation aliasing missed by the online
  `MemoryPressureTracker`.
- Retain the earliest trial achieving the lowest `HeapSimulator` peak if later
  retries with tighter `0.9x` limits do not reduce peak heap usage.

head_commit.message:
[TSL] Use non-const CRTP parameter in ReferenceCounted for RCReference<const T>

Remove the ReferenceCounted<const SubClass> specialization. The CRTP parameter
must always be the plain derived type; constness belongs to the holder, i.e.
RCReference<const T>, as with std::shared_ptr<const T> and
boost::intrusive_ptr<const T>.

Make AddRef()/DropRef()/Destroy() const and the reference counter mutable in
the primary template (same as boost::intrusive_ref_counter), so every
ReferenceCounted type can be managed via RCReference<const T>. Reject
ReferenceCounted<const T> with a static_assert.

name: CI
display_title: #HloDiff Don't let bottom-up matching steal nodes from exact-operand counterparts.

head_commit.message:
#HloDiff Don't let bottom-up matching steal nodes from exact-operand counterparts.

GreedyLimitedCandidatesBottomUpMatcher maps left nodes greedily in post order.
A left node without a real counterpart (e.g. its opcode changed) could take a
right node whose operands are all mapped to the operands of another, still
unmatched left node. That node then fell back to a worse candidate, causing a
cascade of wrong mappings.

A candidate is now skipped if its operands are not mapped exactly to the left
node's operands, but are mapped exactly to those of another unmatched left node
with the same opcode.

Pass an allocation index to MemoryDebugAnnotation::pending_shape_func.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Simplify tile offset indexing map unconditionally.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Simplify tile offset indexing map unconditionally.

***Problem:*** `EmitterContext::EvaluateTilingParameters` only simplifies `offset_indexing_map` when `tile_constraints` is non-empty, leaving redundant schedule constraints in the map domain when `num_tiles` is an exact multiple of `num_tiles_per_pid`.

***Solution:*** Call `offset_indexing_map.Simplify()` unconditionally in `EmitterContext::EvaluateTilingParameters` while keeping `preserve_result_ranges` gated on non-empty `tile_constraints` so redundant domain bounds are canonicalized away without changing result range annotations.

Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

Dispatching executables with many outputs currently invokes `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` and constructs a debug-annotation closure once per non-aliased output leaf, while `ExecuteOptions::use_output_arena` couples all output buffer lifetimes to the longest-lived output.

name: CI
display_title: Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

head_commit.message:
Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

Previously, the MLIR-generated GPU `Pow` kernel lowered `stablehlo.power` to a Linalg/SCF exponentiation-by-squaring loop with a hardcoded upper bound of 6 iterations, which only inspected the lowest 6 bits of the exponent (`y % 64`) and discarded bits at positions >= 6. As a result, odd bases with exponents >= 64 (such as `(-47)**66`) and even bases with exponents >= 64 produced incorrect results on GPU compared to CPU and NumPy fixed-width two's-complement wrap-around semantics.

Update the integer `Pow` exponentiation-by-squaring loop upper bound from 6 to the integer element bit-width so all exponent bits are processed.

Fixes #118202

name: CI
display_title: Update HloCallableInstruction aliasing across operand mutations

head_commit.message:
Update HloCallableInstruction aliasing across operand mutations

Consider an in-place fusion or custom-call that aliases its output to operand 2
while another operand is fused in, permuted, or removed as dead:

```hlo
neg1 = f32[8] negate(p1)
fus = f32[8] fusion(p0, neg1, p2), kind=kCustom, calls=fused_comp,
    output_to_operand_aliasing={{}: (2, {})}
```

Today `CloneAndAppendInstructionIntoCalledComputation` and
`PermuteFusionOperands` in `xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instructions.cc`, along with
`HloComputation::CleanupUnusedOperandsAndParameters` (`RemoveParameter`) in
`xla/hlo/ir/hlo_computation.cc`, mutate operands or wrap a single-output root
into a tuple without updating `output_to_operand_aliasing()`. The stale operand
or output `ShapeIndex` then fails `HloVerifier` when in-place fusions absorb
producers or drop dead parameters.

Update those three mutation paths to erase alias entries referencing a removed
operand, shift higher operand indices down, apply the operand permutation table,
and prepend tuple index 0 when wrapping a single-output root into a tuple.
Verified by `//xla/hlo/ir:hlo_instruction_test`
(`HloInstructionTest.CallableOutputToOperandAliasingUpdatedAcrossMutations`).

name: CI
display_title: Support 64-bit offsets and indices in SPMD partitioning for large shapes.

head_commit.message:
Support 64-bit offsets and indices in SPMD partitioning for large shapes.

Replaces hardcoded S32 offset and index calculations with S64 when tensor dimensions or indices exceed the 32-bit integer limit. This updates partition offset generation, masking logic, and constants across SPMD partitioning to avoid integer overflow on large tensors:
- Infrastructure: adds GetOffsetType and uses it in MakePartitionOffsets to dynamically determine offset types (S32 vs S64) based on tensor dimension bounds.
- Resharding, windowed inputs, and padding: uses 64-bit offsets and index calculations when tensors or padded dimensions exceed 32 bits.
- Gather, scatter, and dot: handles 64-bit operand indices, slice sizes, and contracting/batch dimension offsets.
- DynamicSliceCollectiveBroadcast: accepts integral scalar indices (including S64/U64), lifts 32-bit dimension bounds for 64-bit indices, types local offsets/constants to the index element type, and converts owner to S32 for conditional branch indexing.
- DynamicUpdateSlice: preserves 64-bit index precision without narrowing to S32, promotes partition offsets and update constants to the index type, and ensures select operands match.
- SelectAndScatter: promotes window slice offsets and constants to S64 when dimensions or ordinals require 64 bits, ensuring uniform dynamic-slice start index types.
- PadRotateRightConcat: promotes iota and select boundaries to U64 when padded dimensions exceed 32 bits.
- FFT partitioning: matches dynamic slice offset zero constants to the calculated concat offset type.
- Custom-call (ragged all-to-all and halo exchange): promotes start indices and offsets to 64-bit for dimensions exceeding 32-bit limits.
- Partial reduce: handles 64-bit tensor dimensions and offsets.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014823600

name: CI
display_title: Fill only the padding when linearizing tiled arrays.

head_commit.message:
Fill only the padding when linearizing tiled arrays.

`TiledLinearizer::LinearizeUsingTransposeInto` filled the whole destination buffer with the padding word whenever the array had any padding, and `TransposePlan::Execute` then overwrote almost all of it with the elements. This single-threaded fill runs before the possibly multi-threaded transpose and doubles the memory traffic of linearization.

Fill only the bytes that the transpose does not write: everything but the complete tiles for 2D tilings, everything but each row's elements for 1D tilings, and everything past the elements for rank-1 or untiled arrays. The geometry comes from the `TransposePlan`, and if it disagrees with `TransposePlan::OutputNumElems()` the whole buffer is filled as before. Zero padding is written with `memset`, and NaN padding keeps its previous byte pattern, so the output is bit-identical. The scratch buffer used for sub-tile packed sub-byte types is no longer pre-filled either.

New tests linearize into buffers that initially hold the padding pattern or one of two poison patterns and require identical bytes, so any byte that is left unwritten fails them.

name: CI
display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
executable passes a factory to the new `Executable` constructor, and
`Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module with it the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module, which the executable shares
with the factory.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012082361

name: CI
display_title: Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

head_commit.message:
Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

`Executable` takes its `HloModule` in the constructor and never changes it.
But we want `GpuExecutable` to build its module from a serialized module only
when something needs it (e.g. the profiler), and once that happened the module
should be visible through `has_module()`, `module()` and `shared_module()` like
any other module.

So this change adds a second `Executable` constructor that takes an
`HloModuleFactory` instead of a module, and `Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule`,
which returns the module and builds it with the factory if needed. The factory
is called at most once, even with concurrent callers, and if it fails every
later call returns the same error. After a successful build `has_module()`
returns true. The accessors do an acquire load of a raw pointer to the module
and only look at the `shared_ptr` once that pointer is non-null (it never
changes after that), so the read path doesn't need a lock. (We can't use
`std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>` since XLA still has to build with C++17.)

The lazy state lives in a separate heap allocation, so executables that get
their module in the constructor don't pay for it and behave exactly as before.
There is also a new `Executable(std::nullptr_t)` constructor, since
`Executable(nullptr)` would be ambiguous otherwise.

Pass DebugOptions by reference to GpuExecutableBufferAllocator

`GpuExecutableBufferAllocator::Create` and `GpuExecutableVaRemapAllocator` took
a `const DebugOptions*` and fell back to `ALWAYS_UPDATE` if it was null. That

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Adds StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator, which returns a
MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die)
of the device. The CUDA implementation creates the physical memory with
cuMemCreate, using location type CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN
(CUDA 13.4 and newer). It rejects out-of-range domain ids, older CUDA
versions, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false), and never falls back to
whole-device memory.

name: CI
display_title: Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

head_commit.message:
Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

When a multi-model TPU inference server is under heavy concurrency and hits its
max in-flight computation limit (`max_inflight_computations_semaphore_`),
incoming requests block on `xla::Semaphore::Acquire`. Because `Acquire` waited
on `absl::Mutex::LockWhen` without tracking arrival order, releasing capacity
woke arbitrary waiting threads rather than the oldest waiting request, allowing
newly arrived requests to repeatedly jump ahead of older requests and causing
severe tail-latency starvation.

Track blocked callers in an intrusive arrival-order queue on stack-allocated
`CanAcquireArgs` nodes so the earliest satisfiable waiter is woken first.

Tested with `bazel test //xla/pjrt:semaphore_test`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014141776

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Preserve OriginalValue tracking across Shardy shard_map and sharding annotations.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve OriginalValue tracking across Shardy shard_map and sharding annotations.

When lowering `shard_map` and sharding constraints with Shardy and SPMD partitioning, `OriginalValue` tracking lost value correspondence for instructions inside manual regions and instructions wrapped by identity sharding custom calls:

1. Shardy exported `sdy.manual_computation` bodies and late-inlined manual calls as non-synthetic HLO `call` instructions (or dropped empty `call_hierarchy = ""` when serializing synthetic `OriginalValue` attributes from MLIR to HLO), and `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::SetPartitionedHlo` cleared `original_value` on manual instructions including synthetic manual `call` wrappers. When `CallInliner` subsequently inlined those manual calls, callee instructions were prefixed with a nonexistent call scope or lost synthetic scope correspondence, and `PopulateCallMapForCallLikeInstruction` parsed an empty `""` synthetic `call_hierarchy` into a spurious `{""}` scope entry instead of an empty scope list.
2. Shardy sharding propagation converts unary identity `@Sharding` and `@xla.sdy.PropagationBarrier` custom calls into `sdy.sharding_constraint` and `sdy.propagation_barrier` operations that are later erased or rewritten into reshards without recording an entry in `OriginalValueRecoveryTable`, leaving downstream consumers unable to recover the original array of the eliminated custom call from its operand.

Fix both paths across `xla/service/spmd/shardy/`, `xla/service/spmd/spmd_partitioner.cc`, `xla/hlo/ir/`, `xla/hlo/builder/xla_builder.cc`, `xla/hlo/translate/mhlo_to_hlo/attribute_exporter.cc`, and `xla/hlo/utils/hlo_original_value_analysis.cc`:

name: CI
display_title: Fix grouped convolution partitioning with partially replicated sharding.

head_commit.message:
Fix grouped convolution partitioning with partially replicated sharding.

When a grouped convolution has contracting dimensions partitioned with partial replication across other mesh axes, PartitionConvolutionWithSpatialDimensionHaloExchangeOnLHS/RHS previously all-reduced over all devices in the mesh, multiplying the result by the size of the replicated axis.

We now allow partitioned contracting feature dimensions when feature_group_count == 1 and pass them along with any partitioned spatial dimensions to AllReduceAlongShardingDims. This restricts the all-reduce to only reduce across the partitioned dimensions instead of all devices in the mesh, avoiding both over-reduction on replicated axes and falling back to expensive AllGather on activations.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fuse identical-window collective-permutes on paired (hi, lo) operands in CollectivePermuteCSE.

When `xla_enable_enzyme_comms_opt` is enabled and 64-bit floating-point values are decomposed into `(hi, lo)` pairs (via `X64SplitLow`/`X64SplitHigh`, `FastTwoSum`/`TwoSum`, or adjacent tuple elements), halo exchanges emit two `collective-permute` instructions with identical `source_target_pairs` and slice windows on the paired `hi` and `lo` arrays. Teach `CollectivePermuteCSE` to concatenate the two sliced operands along dimension 0, issue a single array `collective-permute`, and slice the result back into the `hi` and `lo` halves.

name: CI
display_title: Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

head_commit.message:
Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

A deserialized GpuExecutable still needs the HLO module to compute the module fingerprint and to decide whether collectives should use minimal GPU resources. Both are pure functions of the optimized module, so we can compute them at compile time and store them in `GpuExecutableProto` (xla/service/gpu/gpu_executable.proto) instead.

This change adds the `fingerprint` and `collective_use_minimal_resource` fields, writes them in `ToProto` and uses them in `FromProto`. `GpuExecutable::Create` computes the fingerprint from the module unless it's passed in, which happens when deserializing and when the compiler doesn't embed the module. Executables serialized before these fields existed fall back to computing the values from the HLO module, which is still deserialized eagerly for now. Executables without an HLO module have an empty fingerprint and always write `collective_use_minimal_resource=false`, which is the value they used before. If `Params::hlo_module` only holds the serialized module (nothing does that yet), `Create` requires `collective_use_minimal_resource` to be set, because we don't want to build the module just for that and silently using false could differ from what the module would give.

Computing the fingerprint eagerly costs 0.1-0.45% of the JIT compile time (measured on H100 for gemma4_2b, maxtext and a chain of 500 dots, with and without autotuning). That's cheap enough to not justify a lazily computed and cached value.

The fingerprint stored at compile time matches the fingerprint of the module after a serialization round trip (which is what PjRt computed for deserialized executables so far). A new PjRt test checks that for a few non-trivial programs, and I also verified it for all GPU AOT goldens.

The AOT golden comparison ignores both fields since they are derived from the HLO module, which is already ignored.

name: CI
display_title: Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

`GpuExecutable` read the runtime `DebugOptions`, the `partition_size` and the
static device assignment from the `HloModuleConfig` of its `HloModule`. Without
a module it silently fell back to hard-coded values. That ties execution to the
module, which we want to stop building for loaded executables.

So this change stores the debug options and the static device assignment in
`GpuExecutable` instead. For JIT compiled executables they come from the module
config, and `FromProto` reads them straight from `hlo_module_with_config.config`
(including the fallback to `HloModuleProto.device_assignment` that
`HloModule::CreateFromProto` does). The execution path, the buffer allocator,
the module annotations and the static device assignment check now use the
stored values. The per-flag precedence between compile-time and load-time
options is unchanged and now documented next to the new members.

`CommandBufferConversionPass` now gets the slice size explicitly. It comes from
the `GpuTopology` of the executable, which is also where the compiler takes the
`partition_size` from. Executables serialized before `GpuExecutableProto` had a
`gpu_topology` don't have a topology, so for those we still use the serialized
`partition_size`.

The stored options are a copy taken in `GpuExecutable::Create`, while before
every execution read the live module config. I found no code that changes the
debug options of an executable's module after `Create`, so this doesn't change
anything in practice.

Executables without a module config behave differently now. They ran without
any debug options, so the execution code fell back to hard-coded values. Most of
them match the flag defaults, but one doesn't: without options the communication
streams didn't get the highest priority, while
`xla_gpu_enable_highest_priority_async_stream` defaults to true. Now these
executables use the options passed to `GpuExecutable::Create`. So they get
highest-priority communication streams, and runtime flags set by the user (e.g.
NCCL channels or rendezvous timeouts) take effect for them, like they already do
for executables with a module. That affects two paths:

1. JIT compilation with `xla_embed_hlo_module=false`, where `GpuCompiler`
   passes the compile-time options of the module.
2. `GpuExecutable::FromProto` with a proto without `hlo_module_with_config`
   (which is what such an executable serializes to), where these are the
   load-time options.

Executables with a module behave as before.

Also remove the unused `module_id` parameter of `ExecuteThunksImpl`, and pass
the debug options as a reference, since they are never null anymore.

name: CI
display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

display_title: PR #52246: [XLA:GPU] Provision and select locality-domain streams at execution

head_commit.message:
PR #52246: [XLA:GPU] Provision and select locality-domain streams at execution

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52246

📝 Summary of Changes

Runs locality-domain regions on dedicated streams at execution time, builds on [#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124).

- `Backend`: keeps a `StreamPool` per executor and locality domain, created with `StreamExecutor::CreateStreamInLocalityDomain`.
- `ServiceExecutableRunOptions` exposes a borrower for them, passed by `LocalClient`, `Service` and `HloRunner`.
- `GpuExecutable`: finds the locality domains referenced by its `AsyncStartThunk`s, validates them against the compiled and runtime locality-domain counts, and leases one stream per domain for the execution.
- `Thunk::ExecuteParams`: carries the leased streams in `locality_domain_streams`.
- `AsyncStartThunk`: runs locality-domain regions on the leased stream, replacing the `Unimplemented` placeholder from #51737.
- `CudaStream`: records the green context a stream was created in, and exposes it through `green_context()`.

🎯 Justification

This PR connects the stream building blocks from [#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124) to execution, so an XLA program can run selected regions on a specific locality domain.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution. Annotating computations to run on a domain comes in a follow-up PR.

🧪 Unit Tests

`GpuExecutableLocalityDomainTest`:
- `NoReferencesDoNotInvokeLocalityBorrower`: programs without locality-domain regions never borrow.
- `ReferencedDomainRequiresSupportedCounts`, `NegativeCompileLocalityCountIsRejected`, `RuntimeWithoutLocalityDomainsReportsUnsupported`, `CompileRuntimeCountMismatchRejectsDomainOutsideSmallerCount`: count validation.
- `MissingBorrowerIsRejected`, `OutOfRangeDomainIdIsRejected`, `BorrowerErrorIsPropagatedWithContext`: error paths.
- `NestedDuplicateDomainsDeduplicateAndKeepLeaseAlive`: one lease per domain, held for the whole execution.

Also:
- `GpuExecutableRuntimeTest.LocalityDomainStreamsAreExcludedFromGenericStreamCounts`: locality-domain streams don't inflate the compute and communication stream counts.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainStreamSelection`: the nested thunks run on the stream leased for their domain.

## 🧪 Execution Tests

These run on a single GPU, and skip on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.

- `GpuExecutableLocalityDomainTest.BackendPoolsSeparateReuseAndInjectGreenContextStreams`: `Backend` pools stay separate per domain and reuse returned streams; regions on two domains execute on streams in different green contexts.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainsExecuteIndependentDefaultMemoryReadsAndSynchronize`: two locality-domain regions read the same buffer and copy it on their own domain's streams; checks the streams used and the results.

- `GpuExecutableRuntimeTest.LocalityDomainStreamsAreExcludedFromGenericStreamCounts`: locality-domain streams don't inflate the compute and communication stream counts.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainStreamSelection`: the nested thunks run on the stream leased for their domain.

These run on a single GPU, and skip on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.

- `GpuExecutableLocalityDomainTest.BackendPoolsSeparateReuseAndInjectGreenContextStreams`: `Backend` pools stay separate per domain and reuse returned streams; regions on two domains execute on streams in different green contexts.

name: CI
display_title: Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff cquery tag filters

head_commit.message:
Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff cquery tag filters

`Build.bazel_command` always appends `-manual` to `--build_tag_filters` when running a test or build with a `bazel-diff` target pattern file, but `get_cquery_command_options` in `build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` did not include `-manual`. Because `cquery --universe_scope` evaluates wildcard patterns without filtering `manual` targets by default, `bazel-diff` analyzed `manual` targets (such as GPU backend `test_suite` rules on CPU jobs) and included them in the impacted targets list.

So this change appends `-manual` to `--build_tag_filters` in `get_cquery_command_options`. Also, in `xla/tests/build_defs.bzl`, it forwards `tags + ["manual"]` to the fallback empty `strict_cc_test` in `xla_test` when `test_names` is empty, matching the `test_suite` branch.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] [2/2] Unroll and vectorize kLoop reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] [2/2] Unroll and vectorize kLoop reductions.

***Problem:*** `kLoop` fusions that loop over a small reduction dimension (e.g. split-K factors below the warp size) never get vectorized loads and stores, because the unroll factor is sized only from the small output element count and `VectorizeLoadsAndStoresPass` runs before the inner reduction loop is unrolled, so it only sees that non-unit-stride loop.

***Solution:*** Allow unrolling up to `MaxUnrollFactor` (while keeping enough threads to fill the GPU) when the fusion contains a `kReduce` whose operand alone can saturate the GPU, unroll only the inner reduction loops before `VectorizeLoadsAndStoresPass` so the outer unroll loop becomes the innermost vectorizable loop, and teach `lower_tensors` to infer access alignment from `xla.apply_indexing` indices.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] [1/2] Sink reduce through unstrided slice consumers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] [1/2] Sink reduce through unstrided slice consumers.

***Problem:*** When split-K rewriting of a packed `dot` (e.g. a combined QKV projection) produces one `reduce` whose output is split by unstrided `slice` ops into tensors with incompatible downstream shapes, `PriorityFusion` can fuse the `reduce` into only one branch while the other falls back to a `kLoop` fusion.

***Solution:*** In `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier`, when every consumer of a `reduce` is an unstrided `slice` (optionally behind one unary elementwise op) and the slices together cover no more elements than the `reduce` output, replace each `slice` with a `reduce` over the correspondingly sliced input so every branch forms its own reduction fusion without reducing or reading more elements.

name: CI
display_title: Fix grouped convolution partitioning with partially replicated sharding.

head_commit.message:
Fix grouped convolution partitioning with partially replicated sharding.

When a grouped convolution has contracting dimensions partitioned with partial replication across other mesh axes, PartitionConvolutionWithSpatialDimensionHaloExchangeOnLHS/RHS previously all-reduced over all devices in the mesh, multiplying the result by the size of the replicated axis.

We now allow partitioned contracting feature dimensions when feature_group_count == 1 and pass them along with any partitioned spatial dimensions to AllReduceAlongShardingDims. This restricts the all-reduce to only reduce across the partitioned dimensions instead of all devices in the mesh, avoiding both over-reduction on replicated axes and falling back to expensive AllGather on activations.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013501847

name: CI
display_title: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

head_commit.message:
[XTile][RaggedDot] Unify ragged-dot backend selection

Backend selection is now a single function, SelectRaggedDotBackend(), in
xla/service/gpu/ir_emission_utils, the shared utility both passes already
depend on (no pass includes another pass's header).  It applies the
priority order once:

  1a. cuDNN        - IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot()
  1b. hipBLASLt    - IsGpublasLtSupportedGroupedMatMul()
  2.  Triton XTile - IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot()
  3.  default      - expand into a regular dot

CanBeHandledByCuDNNFusion() moved to ir_emission_utils as
IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot(), together with SupportsCudnnRaggedDotWgrad()
and the cuDNN version constants, and now reuses IsRaggedDotWgrad()
instead of a private copy of the ragged-mode classification.

Other changes:

- GpuFloatSupport::SupportsMixedPrecisions() did not accept kRaggedDot,
  so FloatNormalization converted the operands of a bf16 x bf16 -> f32
  ragged-dot even though the XTile path supports it.
- IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() accepted the FP8 types on any target.  The
  OCP formats need Hopper or later on NVIDIA and OCP FP8 support on ROCm;
  the nanoo formats need nanoo FP8 support, i.e. gfx942.
- VerifyTritonConstraints() did not apply the MMA dimension limit to
  kRaggedDot.  The group_sizes operand is excluded: it is read from its
  buffer rather than as an MMA operand and its tile may span all groups.
- IsGenericTritonFusion() now excludes ragged-dot fusions.  They have a
  fixed structure that the emitter relies on, so PriorityFusion must not
  fuse into them; it otherwise fused the group_sizes producer in and the
  emitter failed to resolve it to a buffer argument.
- SchedulingAnnotationsConfig() dropped the scheduling annotation of a
  ragged-dot fusion because it only kept kTritonGemmFusionKind ones.
- TritonFusionNumericsVerifier cannot build a reference module for a
  ragged-dot (nothing lowers a bare kRaggedDot), so it skips them.

display_title: PR #52290: [ROCm][IFRT IR] Accept the ROCm platform in IFRT IR compilation passes

head_commit.message:
PR #52290: [ROCm][IFRT IR] Accept the ROCm platform in IFRT IR compilation passes

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52290

📝 Summary of Changes

`IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass` and `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass`
recognize only the TPU, CUDA and CPU platforms (plus `host` in the verifier). So
compiling an IFRT IR program whose atom programs run on ROCm devices fails:
- `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass::initialize` logs `Unsupported platform: rocm`
  and fails.
- `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass` reports
  `'ifrt.Call' op Unsupported platform for call op: rocm`.
`BasicAtomProgramCompiler` already accepts `rocm`, so these two passes were the only
blockers. This change accepts `xla::RocmName()` wherever `xla::CudaName()` is accepted.

🎯 Justification

Found while compiling Shardy MPMD programs (lowered with `jaxlib._sdy_mpmd.lower_to_ifrt`)
with `IfrtIrProgramCompiler` on the ROCm PJRT plugin.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply:
✨ New Feature,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Please measure and include speedups for one of the public HLOs in
`compiler/xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo/`.

🧪 Unit Tests:
`ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency.mlir`: two ROCm devices added to the platform mapping. An all-ROCm call passes, and calls mixing ROCm with CPU or with CUDA report the single-platform error. The out-of-range case moves to device 9.
New RUN line in `ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir` with `platform_names=rocm,rocm`, reusing the existing Shardy checks.

`bazel test //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency.mlir.test //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir.test`

Both pass. With the pass changes reverted, both fail with the errors above.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

ReadBlock allocates the block size stored in a BlockHandle before it
reads the block. Table::Open and Table::BlockReader pass it handles read
from the file without comparing them with the file size, so a 48-byte
table can request a buffer of several terabytes.

Store the file size in Table::Rep and reject, with DataLoss, any handle
whose block and trailer do not lie within the file before calling
ReadBlock.

name: CI
display_title: Add cuda-only and gpu tags to //xla/tsl/cuda stub rules

head_commit.message:
Add cuda-only and gpu tags to //xla/tsl/cuda stub rules

The `textual_hdrs` attribute on the CUDA stub `cc_library` targets in `//xla/tsl/cuda` unconditionally references the generated `.inc` files from `cuda_stub`. When `bazel-diff` or a non-CUDA build analyzes these targets on unsupported platforms (such as Windows CPU), Bazel configures the underlying `{}_stub_gen` genrule, whose default `select` branch runs a dummy command that fails when executed.

This change adds `cuda-only` and `gpu` tags to the `cc_library` and `alias` targets in `xla/tsl/cuda/BUILD.bazel`, and marks the `{}_stub_gen` genrule in `xla/tsl/cuda/stub.bzl.oss` with `cuda-only`, `gpu`, and `manual`. This way non-CUDA builds with `--build_tag_filters=-gpu` or `-cuda-only` skip these stub targets entirely.

Also:

1. Move `if_nccl(["//xla/tsl/cuda:nccl"])` from `_tools_on_path` in `xla/lit.bzl` into `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:all_runtime` so CPU and ROCm `lit_test` targets do not depend on `nccl_stub`.
2. Add the missing `gpu` tag to `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:stream_executor_cuda`.
3. Add `cuda-only` and `gpu` tags to `@rmm//:rmm` and `@raft` targets that depend on `//xla/tsl/cuda:cudart`.

head_commit.message:
Add cuda-only and gpu tags to //xla/tsl/cuda stub rules

The `textual_hdrs` attribute on the CUDA stub `cc_library` targets in `//xla/tsl/cuda` unconditionally references the generated `.inc` files from `cuda_stub`. When `bazel-diff` or a non-CUDA build analyzes these targets on unsupported platforms (such as Windows CPU), Bazel configures the underlying `{}_stub_gen` genrule, whose default `select` branch runs a dummy command that fails when executed.

This change adds `cuda-only` and `gpu` tags to the `cc_library` and `alias` targets in `xla/tsl/cuda/BUILD.bazel`, and marks the `{}_stub_gen` genrule in `xla/tsl/cuda/stub.bzl.oss` with `cuda-only`, `gpu`, and `manual`. This way non-CUDA builds with `--build_tag_filters=-gpu` or `-cuda-only` skip these stub targets entirely.

Also:

1. Move `if_nccl(["//xla/tsl/cuda:nccl"])` from `_tools_on_path` in `xla/lit.bzl` into `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:all_runtime` so CPU and ROCm `lit_test` targets do not depend on `nccl_stub`.
2. Add the missing `gpu` tag to `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:stream_executor_cuda`.
3. Add `cuda-only` and `gpu` tags to `@rmm//:rmm` and `@raft` targets that depend on `//xla/tsl/cuda:cudart`.

name: CI
display_title: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

head_commit.message:
[XTile][RaggedDot] Unify ragged-dot backend selection

Backend selection is now a single function, SelectRaggedDotBackend(), in
xla/service/gpu/ir_emission_utils, the shared utility both passes already
depend on (no pass includes another pass's header).  It applies the
priority order once:

  1a. cuDNN        - IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot()
  1b. hipBLASLt    - IsGpublasLtSupportedGroupedMatMul()
  2.  Triton XTile - IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot()
  3.  default      - expand into a regular dot

CanBeHandledByCuDNNFusion() moved to ir_emission_utils as
IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot(), together with SupportsCudnnRaggedDotWgrad()
and the cuDNN version constants, and now reuses IsRaggedDotWgrad()
instead of a private copy of the ragged-mode classification.

Other changes:

- GpuFloatSupport::SupportsMixedPrecisions() did not accept kRaggedDot,
  so FloatNormalization converted the operands of a bf16 x bf16 -> f32
  ragged-dot even though the XTile path supports it.
- IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() accepted the FP8 types on any target.  The
  OCP formats need Hopper or later on NVIDIA and OCP FP8 support on ROCm;
  the nanoo formats need nanoo FP8 support, i.e. gfx942.
- VerifyTritonConstraints() did not apply the MMA dimension limit to
  kRaggedDot.  The group_sizes operand is excluded: it is read from its
  buffer rather than as an MMA operand and its tile may span all groups.
- IsGenericTritonFusion() now excludes ragged-dot fusions.  They have a
  fixed structure that the emitter relies on, so PriorityFusion must not
  fuse into them; it otherwise fused the group_sizes producer in and the
  emitter failed to resolve it to a buffer argument.
- SchedulingAnnotationsConfig() dropped the scheduling annotation of a
  ragged-dot fusion because it only kept kTritonGemmFusionKind ones.
- TritonFusionNumericsVerifier cannot build a reference module for a
  ragged-dot (nothing lowers a bare kRaggedDot), so it skips them.

display_title: Allow regular fusion of do_not_duplicate operands with a single user.

head_commit.message:
Allow regular fusion of do_not_duplicate operands with a single user.

`InstructionFusion::ComputeGloballyUnfusible` analyzes the unfused HLO graph up front and marks multi-input operations as `do_not_duplicate` when an expensive downstream operation currently has multiple unfused consumers. Later during fusion, those downstream consumers can merge into a single fusion instruction, leaving the upstream operation with only that one fusion as its consumer.

Check `FusionWouldDuplicate` before blocking regular fusion on `do_not_duplicate` so operations that no longer need to be duplicated can fuse into their sole consumer instead of materializing intermediate buffers.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Autotune generic Triton fusions over the cost model's top-k configs

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Autotune generic Triton fusions over the cost model's top-k configs

Generic Triton fusions (kind __triton, e.g. from SoftmaxRewriterTriton and
PriorityFusion) keep the cost model's top-1 block-level config and were never
autotuned, even with xla_gpu_fusion_autotune_top_k_configs > 1.

With top-k > 1, ConfigAssignerPass now autotunes them if the fusion
autotuner and the block-level emitter backend are enabled.
BlockLevelEmitterBackend supports them and offers the cost model's top-k
configs, falling back to the pre-existing config if the tiling search finds no configs.

With top-k == 1 (the default), compilation output is unchanged.

head_commit.message:
PR #52290: [ROCm][IFRT IR] Accept the ROCm platform in IFRT IR compilation passes

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52290

📝 Summary of Changes

`IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass` and `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass`
recognize only the TPU, CUDA and CPU platforms (plus `host` in the verifier). So
compiling an IFRT IR program whose atom programs run on ROCm devices fails:
- `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass::initialize` logs `Unsupported platform: rocm`
  and fails.
- `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass` reports
  `'ifrt.Call' op Unsupported platform for call op: rocm`.
`BasicAtomProgramCompiler` already accepts `rocm`, so these two passes were the only
blockers. This change accepts `xla::RocmName()` wherever `xla::CudaName()` is accepted.

🎯 Justification

Found while compiling Shardy MPMD programs (lowered with `jaxlib._sdy_mpmd.lower_to_ifrt`)
with `IfrtIrProgramCompiler` on the ROCm PJRT plugin.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply:
✨ New Feature,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Please measure and include speedups for one of the public HLOs in
`compiler/xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo/`.

🧪 Unit Tests:
`ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency.mlir`: two ROCm devices added to the platform mapping. An all-ROCm call passes, and calls mixing ROCm with CPU or with CUDA report the single-platform error. The out-of-range case moves to device 9.
New RUN line in `ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir` with `platform_names=rocm,rocm`, reusing the existing Shardy checks.

`bazel test //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency.mlir.test //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir.test`

Both pass. With the pass changes reverted, both fail with the errors above.

name: CI
display_title: Fix CPU CppGen intrinsic ABI adaptation, inlining, and vectorization.

head_commit.message:
Fix CPU CppGen intrinsic ABI adaptation, inlining, and vectorization.

When CppGen bitcode libraries such as `eigen_unary_32_ll` are compiled without host `-mavx`, SysV x86-64 lowers 256-bit vectors like `<4 x double>` to indirect `ptr byval(<4 x double>)` parameters and stamps host `target-cpu` and `target-features` attributes onto the bitcode functions. Linking those bitcode definitions into an AVX kernel module caused `AlwaysInlinerPass` to skip inlining due to mismatched `target-cpu`/`target-features` attributes, leaving ABI-mismatched calls or un-inlined stack `alloca` adapters (https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49479). Additionally, under `-DEIGEN_VECTORIZE_GENERIC`, Eigen defines only a single packet size (`EIGEN_GENERIC_VECTOR_SIZE_BYTES`), causing narrower sub-packet vector intrinsics and scalar `pmadd` under `EIGEN_SCALAR_MADD_USE_FMA=1` to emit external libm calls (`atan`, `tanh`, `fma`).

Strip host CPU, feature, unwind, and stack-protector attributes when linking CppGen bitcode in `LinkIntoModule`, propagate the destination module's `target-cpu` and `target-features` to linked definitions and `CreateDirectAdapter` wrappers, mark direct adapters for always-inlining, and drop unused external declarations prior to linking. Run `SROAPass` before `InstCombinePass` in `RunInlineAndOptPasses` so stack `alloca`s introduced by ABI adapters are promoted to registers, and provide direct vector/scalar rational approximations in `eigen_unary.cc` so all 16-, 32-, and 64-byte bitcode modules remain free of external libm declarations.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014665180

head_commit.message:
PR #51932: [XLA:CPU] Gate broadcast division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51932

📝 Summary of Changes
Modified the check for the optimization to rewrite A / broadcast(B) to A * broadcast(1 / B)
only when fast math is enabled.
Keep the original division when fast math is disabled.
Add unit tests for both fast-math enabled and disabled case

🎯 Justification
A * (1 / B) introduces an intermediate rounded reciprocal, so it can produce a different floating-point result from A / B.

When fast math is disabled, the simplifier should preserve the original division semantics. This affects workloads using broadcasted divisors, such as per-row or per-sample scaling.

Resolves #51148.

NA

Updated AlgebraicSimplifierTest to verify:
 - Without fast math, A / broadcast(B) remains a division.
 - With fast math, it is rewritten to A * broadcast(1 / B).
 - Updated ScalarDividePredicate to explicitly enable fast math
    since it relies on the same rewrite.

name: CI
display_title: Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

head_commit.message:
Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

`Executable` takes its `HloModule` in the constructor and never changes it.
But we want `GpuExecutable` to build its module from a serialized module only
when something needs it (e.g. the profiler), and once that happened the module
should be visible through `has_module()`, `module()` and `shared_module()` like
any other module.

So this change adds a second `Executable` constructor that takes an
`HloModuleFactory` instead of a module, and `Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule`,
which returns the module and builds it with the factory if needed. The factory
is called at most once, even with concurrent callers, and if it fails every
later call returns the same error. After a successful build `has_module()`
returns true. The accessors do an acquire load of a raw pointer to the module
and only look at the `shared_ptr` once that pointer is non-null (it never
changes after that), so the read path doesn't need a lock. (We can't use
`std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>` since XLA still has to build with C++17.)

The lazy state lives in a separate heap allocation, so executables that get
their module in the constructor don't pay for it and behave exactly as before.
There is also a new `Executable(std::nullptr_t)` constructor, since
`Executable(nullptr)` would be ambiguous otherwise.
